This change has the potential to cause subtle security bugs in the webserver.  extId in this case is routinely a client-generated parameter.  If that silently now gets promoted to the parent namespace, it might be possible to access objects that weren't intended, or your user shouldn't have access to.

As the code exists on master, the incorrect path would result in an error (usually 404), which gets propagated to the user.  After this patch, now a valid path is formed.

Is there a compelling reason (if you have example of code that would benefit, please share it) to make this promote to the parent object?  I agree, we could handle this case better.  I'd advocate for the resulting path being something like.

/<invalid_path>

as something easy to implement, but doesn't impact existing code.  In a quick test, it does look like std::filesystem will promote an empty append to the parent.  If that's the route we want to go here, the existing bmcweb code will need to be moved to another method, or we need to explicitly check for empty string at every operator/ site that deals with untrusted input (nearly all of them).  Is that a change you're willing to go engineer and propose as part of this patchset?  I'm guessing not, but certainly worth asking


FWIW, I think the cleanest API for the webservers usage of this would be a std::format-like variant and no usage of operator/ at all, but that's a ton of work that I don't want to put on this change trying to make things more correct.

First of all, thanks for all the input here 👍

> Is there a compelling reason (if you have example of code that would benefit, please share it) to make this promote to the parent 
object? 

I never saw a use-case for an append operation `/=` to not append anything. That would make it a maybe-append operation and more complicated for review.

>  In a quick test, it does look like std::filesystem will promote an empty append to the parent.

As per your check, `std::filesystem::path` operates this way but our D-Bus use-case is slightly different. While it is common to find things like config files at different levels in the filesystem tree, D-Bus interface are usually found at a given level of depth. At least currently that is the case for most interfaces.

We cannot let `std::filesystem::path` do our homework here anyways because it appends a trailing `/`.

```cpp
std::filesystem::path path("/xyz/openbmc_project/software");
std::cout << (path / "") << std::endl;

// "/xyz/openbmc_project/software/"
```

> I agree, we could handle this case better.  I'd advocate for 
the resulting path being something like /<invalid_path>

I am ok with this alternative. Appending some error string which clearly describes what went wrong and preserves the user code intent to append a path segment.

Something like

```
sdbusplus::message::object_path path("/xyz/openbmc_project");

path /= "";

// path is now /xyz/openbmc_project/error_empty_string_append
```

This lands us at the user code intended depth and preserves both the namespace path as well as what went wrong.

Kindly review again and check if the new revision is acceptable.

What's there is better than patchset 1, and doesn't cause the security issue.  If it's really what you want, I'm ok with it, but if there's no use case, I have a minor preference for the status quo, which admittedly does cause an invalid object path, but also should never really be called that way, so the invalid object path throwing an exceptino later is "correct"

> so the invalid object path throwing an exceptino later is "correct"

Usually i try to follow these steps

- parse user input
- sanitize user input
- further processing

I don't like issues caused by user input to surface later deep inside some library code when it could have been caught beforehand. The error could appear at a different point in time and can be harder to debug.

If we do it any different then one can never make any assumption about an object path.

I would like to make the assumption that my object path is actually a valid object path (i know, currently we cannot assume it, but maybe some day in the future).

Otherwise it's hard to convince someone to use a class like this if it's just a fancy string wrapper and cannot provide any invariants.

I'll mark this as resolved since you said you're okay with it.

> > so the invalid object path throwing an exceptino later is "correct"
> 
> Usually i try to follow these steps
> 
> - parse user input
> - sanitize user input
> - further processing
> 

As a generalist, I agree with you, but std::filesystem doesn't really seem to operate that way, so if the goal is to follow that API, we need to decide which goal is more important, the above, or doing what stdlib does.

To do the way you want here, we'd need a path to return an error, and the prototype would need to change, maybe we could have an append(str) method that works the way we want?

> I don't like issues caused by user input to surface later deep inside some library code when it could have been caught beforehand. The error could appear at a different point in time and can be harder to debug.
> 
> If we do it any different then one can never make any assumption about an object path.
> 
> I would like to make the assumption that my object path is actually a valid object path (i know, currently we cannot assume it, but maybe some day in the future).

I think this is where we disagree (at this moment).  I could see us implementing an object with "always valid" semantics, but then we need to adjust how we're returning errors to not match std::filesystem, which I believe allows setting an invalid path today.

> 
> Otherwise it's hard to convince someone to use a class like this if it's just a fancy string wrapper and cannot provide any invariants.
> 
> I'll mark this as resolved since you said you're okay with it.

> As a generalist, I agree with you, but std::filesystem doesn't really 
seem to operate that way, so if the goal is to follow that API, we need 
to decide which goal is more important, the above, or doing what stdlib 
does.

I don't see a need to follow `std::filesystem::path` semantics to the letter if it prevents us from implementing D-Bus semantics. `sdbusplus` is a D-Bus abstraction library, not a filesystem abstraction. We should not violate the spec we are implementing without having a very good reason for it.

> I have a minor preference for the status quo, which admittedly does 
cause an invalid object path, but also should never really be called 
that way, so the invalid object path throwing an exceptino later is 
"correct"

I pushed a new revision this time using exceptions since that seems to be the preference here. Please let me know your thoughts and thanks for the feedback so far 👍
